intent: Close the two measured bypasses in the network layer: the VPN provider could be uninstalled, and traffic flowed normally whenever the tunnel was down. Also provision the home coordinates, which turns enforcement from permanent-everywhere into the intended geofence.
scope: Non-goal: locking RethinkDNS's in-app settings, which no device owner API can do
changes: setPackageUninstallBlocked applies uninstall protection to the VPN provider, re-asserted every pass. This was a measured hole, not a hypothetical: `pm uninstall --user 0 com.celzero.bravedns` succeeded while the VPN was pinned and DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN was set, and took the whole filter with it.

setAlwaysOnVpn gained a lockdown parameter, driven by a new vpn_lockdown policy field (default false, so an older asset cannot silently cut the device off). Lockdown drops every packet not going through the tunnel, which is what closes 'turn the VPN off and browse freely'.

releaseDeviceOwner reads the pinned package BEFORE unpinning and then unblocks its uninstall. Reversed, getAlwaysOnVpnPackage returns null after the unpin and the provider would stay permanently unremovable -- the same trap the self-uninstall ordering already avoids.

verification.command: pytest ; gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest ; flutter test ; flutter analyze
verification.evidence: 129 Python tests, 16 Kotlin, 69 Dart, analyze clean.

verification.command: run an enforcement pass, then dumpsys device_policy
verification.evidence: logcat 'alwaysOnVpn -> com.celzero.bravedns' and 'uninstallBlocked(com.celzero.bravedns)=true'; dumpsys reports mAlwaysOnVpnLockdown=true.

verification.command: pm uninstall --user 0 com.celzero.bravedns  (the exact command that removed it earlier)
verification.evidence: Failure [DELETE_FAILED_OWNER_BLOCKED], both via `pm uninstall --user 0` and `adb uninstall`. The package is still installed.

logcat 'home location written'; the Geofence row flipped from 'no home set - enforcing everywhere' to 'active'. The next pass logged 'applied AT_HOME' instead of LOCATION_UNKNOWN, so the geofence is driving the decision from a real fix (network provider, hAcc 15.8m) rather than failing closed.

risks: THE DNS FILTER HAS NO RULES. I uninstalled RethinkDNS while testing whether it was protected -- a destructive command run to answer a question that policy state would have answered -- and its blocklists live in app-private storage, so reinstalling restored the app but not the configuration. youtube.com currently resolves to a real IP. The rules must be re-entered by hand before the network layer means anything.

Lockdown is now on. If RethinkDNS breaks or is force-stopped, the device has no connectivity at all until device ownership is released. That is survivable only because the release path is in the enforcer app and needs no network -- verified on this device while the account count was 0.

RethinkDNS's own settings remain editable: its blocklists can be turned off from inside the app, and no device owner API can prevent that. Its built-in AppLockActivity (biometric/PIN) is the only available mitigation and is the user's to enable.
The AWAY branch is now reachable but still unobserved: the phone has been at home for every pass. Walking outside the 150m radius is the only way to see the always-blocked exemption hold in practice.
rollback: In-app 'Release device owner' unpins the VPN (clearing lockdown), unblocks both the enforcer's and the provider's uninstall, and clears DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN, in that order.
If the device loses connectivity because of lockdown, that button is the fix and it does not need the network.
